Paragraph: Having reached the celestial realm of Heaven, Yudhishthira expected to find his virtuous brothers and Draupadi, but was instead horrified to see Duryodhana seated upon a magnificent throne, glowing with royal splendor. When led further, Yudhishthira was taken down a dark, foul path into the underworld—a place of terrifying sights, burning fires, stench, and the agonizing cries of his beloved brothers and Draupadi weeping in torment. Overwhelmed by profound shock, grief, and righteous anger, Yudhishthira turned to the celestial messenger and declared: 'Go back to those who sent you! I shall not return to Heaven. Here will I stay with my brothers, for their presence makes even this hell a paradise to me.' At that moment, the terrifying illusion dissolved. Dharma Deva appeared, revealing that it was a final test to cleanse Yudhishthira of his last remaining pride and his brief deception regarding Drona's death, assuring him that all his brothers were already resting in eternal glory.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Yudhishthira encounters a final existential shock and moral trial in the afterlife when he finds his enemies enjoying heavenly luxury while his heroic brothers appear trapped in hellish torment.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Yudhishthira demonstrates ultimate loyalty and unyielding compassion, choosing to remain in hell alongside his loved ones to share their suffering rather than enjoy solitary celestial bliss.
Outcome/Resolution: The horrific vision is revealed to be a Maya (cosmic illusion) to purify his soul; Yudhishthira passes the final trial and ascends to true, eternal liberation alongside his family.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Pariksha (The ultimate spiritual test of moral integrity and selflessness)
Maya-Darshana (Experiencing terrifying sensory illusions meant to burn away residual subtle ego)
Nishkama Compassion (Loving devotion that prefers sharing torment with others over solitary enjoyment)
Citta-Shuddhi (Final purification of the mind before complete Moksha)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The Svargarohana Parva illustrates that even the most righteous soul must undergo 'Pariksha' (testing) to eradicate subtle traces of pride and resentment. Yudhishthira's willingness to renounce Heaven for the sake of his loved ones proves that true spiritual realization ('Moksha') transcends personal comfort and rests on boundless, selfless love.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This final chapter represents the resolution of existential trauma and moral ambiguity. Presented with a cognitive dissonance of paradise vs. punishment, Yudhishthira displays supreme value-congruence and emotional resilience—demonstrating that psychological integrity is achieved when one's commitment to empathy and relationships overrides self-serving rewards.
